title: Varun Beverages Ltd - 540180 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Varun Beverages Q1 CY2026 revenue rose 18.1% to Rs 65,742 mn and EBITDA 21% to Rs 15,289 mn on 16.3% volume growth.
summary.overview: Consolidated volumes grew 16.3% to 363.4 mn cases, with India up 14.4% and international up 21.4%, after a weak prior-year summer hit by rains. Consolidated realisation per case rose 1.6% on favourable currency in international markets, while India realisation fell 1.5% on pack upsizing and selective Rs 10 price points. EBITDA margin expanded 55 bps to 23.3% and PAT rose 20.1% to Rs 8,787 mn, though depreciation (+30.9%) and finance cost (+18%) rose on new plants and the Twizza acquisition. Management said it is covered on packaging and raw materials for the current quarter and holds about 6 months of inventory internationally, with the crude-linked cost risk flagged for later quarters.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Volume up 14.4%; realisation down 1.5% on pack upsizing and selective Rs 10 price points; India EBITDA margin up 112 bps on operating efficiencies and gross margin gains.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Volume up 21.4%, with management saying all international markets grew double digits except Morocco; Twizza (South Africa) acquired via BevCo at EV ZAR 2,053 mn.

segments.name: Product mix
segments.commentary: CSD 73.6% of volume, non-carbonated beverages 7.5%, packaged water 18.9%; low/no-sugar products about 63% of consolidated volume. Dairy growing about 60% with realisation near 3x normal; Tropicana PET above 100% growth.

segments.name: Snacks / food distribution (Africa)
segments.commentary: Q1 snack foods revenue Rs 112 cr vs Rs 52 cr in Q1 CY25; Zimbabwe plant commissioned end of last year.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Q2 demand to be better than Q1 if weather holds; said first month of summer 'looks very good'.
India raw material cover is complete for this quarter and partial for next; international inventory about 6 months, so near-term impact described as zero to a couple of points.
Gasoline/transport cost increases expected to be absorbed by reducing discounts and efficiency gains; no major P&L impact expected if volumes hold.
India capex for CY26 expected below Rs 500-600 cr, with only one plant planned.
Management expects double-digit growth in India for the next 5-10 years and international growth not below double digits absent external shocks.
Expects about 500,000 new outlets to be added in CY26 on a base of about 4 mn outlets.
Crickley Dairy acquisition (EV about ZAR 238 mn incl. working capital) subject to regulatory approvals.
capex_capacity: India capex for CY26 to be under Rs 500-600 cr, with only about one new plant; existing capacity seen sufficient to deliver up to 50% growth without new capacity.

Four plants commissioned last year (Buxar, Prayagraj, Damtal, Meghalaya) have stabilised; management says it is no longer opening smaller plants and cost of production in larger plants is about half that of smaller ones.
Twizza revenue about Rs 800 cr (last full year), acquisition price about Rs 1,140 cr; Crickley Dairy revenue about Rs 160 cr; combined about Rs 1,000 cr. Margins not yet guided.
Typical plant payback 3-4 years at around 30% RoCE, per management.
Aluminium cans are under 2% of sales; cans tied up above that level, though shortage in the industry.
demand_pricing: Management says the summer season is strong after a weak prior year, with May and June the key months; April end was 'not great'.
Industry chilling equipment additions of about 1 mn units per year (about 0.5 mn from Campa, Coke and VBL combined plus 0.4-0.5 mn own coolers by outlets).
Rs 10 price point used selectively, under 2% of total volume, to retain distributors.
Competitors (B-brands, water players) have cut discounts rather than raise prices, per management; PET and can shortages affecting the whole industry.
Ad-Rush (Rs 60 mid-priced energy drink) performing well above plan; can shortage constraining supply. Sting Classic launched in cans and PET (April), with early response described as strong.

qa_highlights.question: What is the near-term impact of higher oil prices on packaging and other costs?
qa_highlights.answer: International raw materials impact practically zero to a couple of points given about 6 months inventory; India has minor impact for this quarter and some for next, offset by lower discounts and cost cuts. Transport cost cannot be stocked but is absorbable.

qa_highlights.question: Why did India realisation improve to -1.5% from -4% last quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Premiumisation through new launches and dairy growth of about 60% (realisation near 3x normal) helped, along with lower discounting and efficiency; Rs 10 price points are used selectively.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company placed on aluminium cans and PET supply?
qa_highlights.answer: Cans are under 2% of sales and tied up above that requirement; shortage is industry-wide and customers may switch to PET or glass.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 2-year CAGR slowdown in India a concern?
qa_highlights.answer: Management disputed the 6-8% figure, citing a 23% average CAGR historically; said last year was an exceptional weather-hit year and growth should stay double-digit.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be a margin hit if crude stays high for several quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it holds 6 months inventory and expects competitors to take price increases or absorb the hit first; does not expect to take a hit itself.

qa_highlights.question: Is the upsizing from 250 ml to 400 ml adding consumption, and is India margin affected?
qa_highlights.answer: Consumption is rising both in litres and in units; full-quarter upsizing effects already absorbed by volumes and plant efficiency, with minor upsides to be absorbed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plant payback and utilisation impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Normal payback 3-4 years at around 30% RoCE; higher utilisation is helping as larger lines (1,000 bottles per minute vs 200) replace old high-cost plants.

risks_watch: Crude-linked input cost (PET, gasoline, transport) and aluminium can shortage could pressure margins from Q2 if discounts cannot be cut further.
India realisation may fall further (management said it 'might even become lower') with discounting and pack upsizing.
Weather risk: management says the season depends on rains and any abnormal rain could hurt volumes; prior-year weather hit was severe.
Integration of Twizza and Crickley Dairy: margins not yet disclosed; Crickley subject to regulatory approvals.
Finance cost and depreciation growth (+18% and +30.9%) will weigh on PAT growth relative to EBITDA.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand and summer trends, with an assertive tone on cost cover. Management was evasive on specifics such as Twizza/Crickley margins, future price increases and competitor share, and pushed back on the analyst's 2-year CAGR framing.
key_quotes: We are completely covered for this quarter, and we are partly covered for the next quarter also.
We think other people will blink before we blink, we have to wait and see.
Normally we work on a 3-4 year payback. 30% RoCE.
Water is like a commodity, you can increase your sales as much as you want by offering discounts, which we are not in the game of and that is why we can sustain our margins.

financial_highlights.change: Down from about -4% in Q4 CY25 per analyst; driven by pack upsizing and price-point launches
Four new plants commissioned last year (Buxar, Prayagraj, Damtal, Meghalaya)

adds.what: One new India plant planned for CY26 (capex under Rs 500-600 cr for India)

growth.why: Management guides double-digit India growth for 5-10 years and international growth not below double digits, backed by existing capacity sufficient for up to 50% growth, one planned plant, and ~500,000 new outlets in CY26 on a ~4 mn base; the call gives no order book but the Q1 volume growth of 16.3% supports the outlook.
